name: luno-for-cc
description: LUNO for CC — personal Claude Code chat for Cursor / VS Code.

untrustedWorkspaces.description: Luno spawns the Claude CLI against the open folder and lets an agent read and write its files, so it needs the same trust the folder's own code does. It also holds a Claude subscription credential.

virtualWorkspaces.description: The CLI is a local process that works on a real checkout on disk, which a virtual filesystem does not provide.

commands.title: LUNO: Open Chat in New Tab

luno.model.description: Model passed to 'claude -p --model'. Defaults to a CLI alias (sonnet, opus, haiku, opusplan, default) that always tracks the latest model for that tier; an explicit version (e.g. claude-sonnet-4-6) also works. Applies to new chats — each conversation then carries its own, so changing this never retargets a chat that is already open.

luno.effort.description: Reasoning effort passed to 'claude --effort'. Higher levels let the model reason longer (and spend more tokens) before answering. Set from the model picker in the chat composer. Applies to new chats — each conversation then carries its own, so changing this never retargets a chat that is already open.

luno.thinking.description: Enable extended thinking (sets 'alwaysThinkingEnabled' for the session). When on, the model reasons step-by-step before answering — higher quality on complex work, at a higher token cost. Toggle from the model picker in the chat composer. Applies to new chats — each conversation then carries its own, so changing this never retargets a chat that is already open.

luno.claudeBinaryPath.description: Absolute path to the 'claude' CLI binary Luno runs. Leave empty to auto-detect: Luno searches PATH and the standard install locations (~/.claude/local, npm global, Homebrew). Set this only to pin a specific install, or if auto-detection fails — run 'where claude' (Windows) or 'which claude' to find yours. On Windows point it at claude.exe, not the claude.cmd shim. Model aliases (opus, sonnet, default) resolve to whatever models that binary knows, so a self-updating native install picks up new models without waiting for a Luno release.

luno.devServerUrl.description: Dev only. When set to a running Vite dev server (bun run dev:webview → http://localhost:5173), the panel loads the webview sources from it instead of the built bundle, so UI edits hot-reload instantly — no rebuild, no repackage, no Reload Window. Leave empty for normal use. Note: changes to extension-host code (src/) still need a window reload.

luno.devAutoRestart.description: Dev only. In an Extension Development Host (F5), restart the extension host automatically whenever 'bun run watch' rebuilds dist/extension.js — the closest thing to hot-reload for extension-host code, which VS Code cannot reload in place. Ignored entirely in a normally installed extension.

enumDescriptions: Ask — prompts before every edit and command.
Plan — read-only; drafts a plan and executes nothing.
Agent — auto-applies reversible edits and allow-listed commands; destructive and network commands still prompt.
Bypass — DANGEROUS. No approval prompt for anything, including rm, curl | bash and force-push.
luno.permissionMode.description: Tool approval behavior. 'default' prompts before each action; 'plan' is read-only / no execution; 'auto' auto-approves reversible edits and bash commands matching allowedBashPatterns, while destructive and network commands still prompt. 'bypass' disables the approval gate entirely — the CLI runs every tool without asking, including deletes, arbitrary shell and force-push. Switching into 'bypass' from the panel requires an explicit confirmation, and Shift+Tab never cycles into it. Applies to new chats — each conversation then carries its own, so changing this never retargets a chat that is already open.

luno.autosave.description: Save modified editors before each turn. The CLI reads files from disk, so an unsaved buffer means the agent works from a version of the code you are not looking at. Untitled documents are never saved — that would open a Save As dialog.

luno.respectGitIgnore.description: Use the repository's own ignore rules when listing files for @-mentions, instead of a fixed exclude list. Off falls back to excluding node_modules, dist, build, out, .next, .venv and __pycache__ only — which offers up gitignored files the project deliberately keeps out.

luno.sendDiagnostics.description: Include the editor's Problems (errors and warnings from language servers) with each turn, so the agent can see what your IDE already knows instead of running a compiler through the shell to rediscover it. Errors are sent first and the list is capped.

luno.sendEditorContext.description: Include the file you have open and any highlighted text with each turn, so 'why does this crash?' with a line selected has a subject. Only the selection is sent, capped in size — never the whole file. Off means the agent learns about a selection only when you press Ctrl+U.

luno.useCtrlEnterToSend.description: Require Ctrl+Enter (Cmd+Enter on macOS) to send, leaving plain Enter to insert a newline. For people who write multi-line prompts and lose them to a reflexive Enter. Off keeps Enter as send and Shift+Enter as newline.

luno.terminalCapture.description: Keep the output of the last command run in each terminal, so @terminal: can put it in a prompt. Only terminals with VS Code shell integration are captured, and only commands run after Luno started — the API cannot read a terminal's scrollback. Off captures nothing and leaves @terminal: with an empty list.

luno.maxTokens.description: Max output tokens per assistant turn, passed to the CLI as CLAUDE_CODE_MAX_OUTPUT_TOKENS. 0 leaves the CLI's own default in place. A low cap means fewer rate-limit hits and truncated answers on long edits.

luno.allowedBashPatterns.description: Regex patterns of bash commands auto-approved in auto mode.

enumDescriptions: Every chat works in the folder you have open. Simplest, but parallel chats can overwrite each other and a rewind in one can undo another.
Each chat opened in a tab gets its own git worktree and branch; the sidebar keeps working on the files you have open.
Every chat, including the sidebar, works in its own git worktree. Nothing an agent does appears in your open files until you merge its branch.
luno.worktree.description: Whether a chat gets its own git worktree. Isolation keeps parallel chats from colliding — separate files, separate branch, shared history — at the cost of the work not showing up in your open files until the branch is merged. Worktrees live in .claude/worktrees/ and are removed when the chat closes, unless they still hold uncommitted or unmerged work.

scripts.build: bun run esbuild.config.mjs && bun run --cwd webview build
scripts.lint: bun run lint:types && bun run lint:js && bun run lint:css
scripts.lint:types: tsc --noEmit && tsc --noEmit -p tsconfig.test.json && bun run --cwd webview lint
